translations.literal: Prince of Yan Tan greatly defeated them, displayed Chongzhi and the others, and beheaded more than ten thousand; all Huainan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, Prince of Yan, routed them, displayed Chongzhi and others, beheaded more than ten thousand, and all Huainan submitted.

sentences.zh: 是月，永昌王仁攻懸瓠，拔之，獲義隆守將趙淮，送京師斬之。

translations.literal: That month Prince of Yongchang Ren attacked Xuanchi, took it, captured Yilong's defending general Zhao Huai, and sent him to the capital for execution.
translations.idiomatic: That month Ren took Xuanchi, captured Zhao Huai, Yilong's defender, and sent him to the capital for execution.

sentences.zh: 過定項城，及淮西，大破義隆將劉康祖，斬之，并虜將軍胡盛之、王羅漢等，傳致行宮。

translations.literal: Passing Dingxiang and west of the Huai, he greatly defeated Liu Yilong's general Liu Kangzu, beheaded him, and also captured the generals Hu Shengzhi and Wang Luohan and sent them to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Dingxiang and west of the Huai, he routed Liu Kangzu, beheaded him, and captured Hu Shengzhi and Wang Luohan to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 癸未，車駕臨江，起行宮於瓜步山。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage came to the river; a traveling palace was raised on Mount Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day the court came to the river and raised a traveling palace on Mount Guabu.

sentences.zh: 永昌王仁自歷陽至於江西，高涼王那自山陽至於廣陵，諸軍皆同日臨江，所過城邑，莫不望塵奔潰，其降者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Prince of Yongchang Ren from Liyang to west of the river, Prince of Gaoliang Na from Shanyang to Guangling—all armies on the same day came to the river; every city passed looked to the dust and fled; those who submitted were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Ren from Liyang and Na from Shanyang to Guangling—all reached the river the same day; cities fled at the dust; submissions were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 甲申，義隆使獻百牢，貢其方物，又請進女於皇孫以求和好。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: Yilong sent envoys offering a hundred oxen, presenting local products, and also asking to send a daughter to the imperial grandson to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day Yilong sent envoys with a hundred oxen and local tribute and asked to send a daughter to the imperial grandson for peace.

sentences.zh: 帝以師婚非禮，許和而不許婚，使散騎侍郎夏侯野報之。

translations.literal: The Emperor held that peace by marriage was not ritual; he granted peace but not marriage and sent Palace Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xiahou Ye in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held peace by marriage unritual; he granted peace but not marriage and sent Xiahou Ye in reply.

sentences.zh: 詔皇孫為書致馬通問焉。

translations.literal: An edict that the imperial grandson write a letter sending horses in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the imperial grandson to write sending horses in exchange.

sentences.zh: 夏五月壬寅，大赦。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day renyin: a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the renyin day, there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 六月壬戌，改年。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renxu: the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the sixth month the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 車師國王遣子入侍。

translations.literal: The king of Cheshi sent his son to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Cheshi sent his son to court.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫刑網太密，犯者更眾，朕甚愍之。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When the penal net is too dense, offenders grow ever more numerous—We are deeply moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "When the penal net is too dense, offenders multiply—We are deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 有司其案律令，務求厥中。

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices examine the statutes and commands and strive for the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Let the offices examine the statutes and strive for the mean.

sentences.zh: 自餘有不便於民者，依比增損。

translations.literal: Whatever else is inconvenient for the people, add or reduce by comparison."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever else burdens the people, add or reduce by comparison."

sentences.zh: 」詔太子少傅游雅、中書侍郎胡方回等改定律制。

translations.literal: An edict that Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince You Ya and Secretariat Gentleman Hu Fanghui and others were to revise and fix the law code.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered You Ya, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and Hu Fanghui, Secretariat Gentleman, and others to revise the law code.

sentences.zh: 略陽王羯兒，儀同三司、高涼王那有罪賜死。

translations.literal: Prince of Lueyang Jie'er and Na, Prince of Gaoliang, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, were guilty and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Jie'er, Prince of Lueyang, and Na, Prince of Gaoliang, Equal to the Three Dukes, were guilty and put to death.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，皇太子薨。

translations.literal: Day wuchen: the Crown Prince died.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day the Crown Prince died.

sentences.zh: 壬申，葬景穆太子於金陵。

translations.literal: Day renshen: Emperor Jingmu the Crown Prince was buried at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day the Crown Prince was buried at Jinling as Emperor Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁亥，行幸陰山。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dinghai: the imperial carriage traveled to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the dinghai day, the emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 省諸曹吏員三分之一。

translations.literal: Clerical staff of the various bureaus was reduced by one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical staff of the bureaus was cut by one-third.

sentences.zh: 九月癸巳，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day guisi: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the guisi day, the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月庚辰朔，南來降民五千餘家於中山謀叛，州軍討平之。

translations.literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day gengchen, first day: more than five thousand southern submitter households at Zhongshan plotted rebellion; provincial troops punished and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the new-year gengchen day, more than five thousand southern submitter households at Zhongshan rebelled; provincial troops pacified them.

sentences.zh: 冀州刺史、張掖王沮渠萬年與降民通謀，賜死。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jizhou, Prince of Zhangye Juqu Wannian, conspired with submitters and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian, Prince of Zhangye, Inspector of Jizhou, conspired with submitters and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，帝崩於永安宮，時年四十五。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiayin: the Emperor died at Yong'an Palace at age forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the jiayin day, the Emperor died at Yong'an Palace at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 祕不發喪，中常侍宗愛矯皇后令，殺東平王翰，迎南安王余入而立之，大赦，改元為永平，尊皇后赫連氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: Death was kept secret; Palace Attendant Zong Ai forged the Empress's order, killed Prince of Dongping Han, welcomed Prince of Nan'an Yu inward and set him up, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the reign title to Yongping, and honored Empress Helian as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Death was kept secret; Zong Ai forged the Empress's order, killed Han, Prince of Dongping, welcomed Yu, Prince of Nan'an, proclaimed amnesty, changed the title to Yongping, and honored Empress Helian as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 三月辛卯，上尊諡曰太武皇帝，葬於雲中金陵，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinmao: the posthumous title Taiwu Emperor was raised; burial was at Yunzhong Jinling; temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the xinmao day, the posthumous title Emperor Taiwu was raised; he was buried at Yunzhong Jinling; temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，劉義隆將檀和之寇濟州，梁坦及魯安生軍于京索，龐萌、薛安都寇弘農。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month: Liu Yilong's general Tan Hezhi raided Jizhou; Liang Tan and Lu Ansheng encamped at Jingsuo; Pang Meng and Xue Andu raided Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer Tan Hezhi of Liu Yilong raided Jizhou; Liang Tan and Lu Ansheng camped at Jingsuo; Pang Meng and Xue Andu raided Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，征南將軍安定公韓元興討之，和之退，梁坦、安生亦走。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: General Who Conquers the South, Duke of Anding Han Yuanxing campaigned against them; Hezhi withdrew, and Liang Tan and Ansheng also fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Han Yuanxing, Duke of Anding, General Who Conquers the South, campaigned against them; Hezhi withdrew and Liang Tan and Ansheng fled.

sentences.zh: 八月，冠軍將軍封禮率騎二千從浢津南渡赴弘農。

translations.literal: Eighth month: General Who Vanquishes the Foe Feng Li led two thousand horse south across from Fuzhou Ford toward Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Feng Li, General Who Vanquishes the Foe, led two thousand horse south from Fuzhou Ford toward Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 九月，司空高平公兒烏干屯潼關，平南將軍昌黎公元遼屯河內。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Minister of Works, Duke of Gaoping Erwugan encamped at Tong Pass; General Who Pacifies the South, Duke of Changli Yuan Liao, encamped at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Erwugan, Duke of Gaoping, Minister of Works, encamped at Tong Pass; Yuan Liao, Duke of Changli, General Who Pacifies the South, at Henei.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙午朔，余為宗愛所賊。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingwu, first day: Yu was murdered by Zong Ai.
translations.idiomatic: On the new-year bingwu day of the tenth month of winter Yu was murdered by Zong Ai.

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書長孫渴侯與尚書陸麗迎立皇孫，是為高宗焉。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Changsun Kehou of the Secretariat and Minister of Works Lu Li welcomed and set up the imperial grandson—this is Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Kehou, Palace Attendant, and Lu Li, Minister of Works, welcomed the imperial grandson—Emperor Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 帝生不逮密太后，及有所識，言則悲慟，哀感傍人，太宗聞而嘉歎。

translations.literal: The Emperor never knew Empress Mi in life; when he came to awareness he spoke with grief and moved those beside him; Taizong heard and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He never knew Empress Mi in life; when he came to awareness he grieved aloud and moved those beside him; Taizong heard and praised him.

sentences.zh: 暨太宗不豫，衣不釋帶。

translations.literal: When Taizong was unwell he did not remove his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was ill he did not remove his belt.

sentences.zh: 性清儉率素，服御飲膳，取給而已，不好珍麗，食不二味，所幸昭儀、貴人，衣無兼綵。

translations.literal: By nature he was pure, frugal, and plain; dress, carriage, food, and drink were only what sufficed; he did not love rarities; he ate no second dish; the favored Ladies of Bright Deportment and Honored Persons wore no multicolored robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was pure and frugal; dress and food sufficed; he loved no luxuries, ate but one dish, and favored consorts wore no multicolored robes.

sentences.zh: 羣臣白帝更峻京邑城隍，以從周易設險之義，又陳蕭何壯麗之說。

translations.literal: The ministers reported to the Emperor that the capital walls and moat should be heightened further, following the Changes in the meaning of setting defenses, and also cited Xiao He's argument for magnificence.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers urged heightening the capital walls per the Changes and cited Xiao He's plea for magnificence.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古人有言，在德不在險。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The ancients had a saying: virtue lies not in defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The ancients said virtue lies not in defenses.

sentences.zh: 屈丐蒸土築城，而朕滅之，豈在城也？

translations.literal: Juqu Qufu steamed earth to build a city, yet We destroyed him—was it in the walls?
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Qufu built walls of steamed earth and We destroyed him—was it the walls?

sentences.zh: 今天下未平，方須民力，土功之事，朕所未為，蕭何之對，非雅言也。

translations.literal: The realm is not yet pacified and We still need the people's strength; earthworks We have not undertaken; Xiao He's reply is not elegant speech."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is not pacified and We need the people's strength; We have not built walls; Xiao He's reply is not fine speech."

sentences.zh: 」每以財者軍國之本，無所輕費，至賞賜，皆是死事勳績之家，親戚受寵未曾橫有所及。

translations.literal: He always held wealth the root of army and state and spent nothing lightly; even in reward it was only households of those who died in service for merit—kinsmen favored never received anything beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: He held wealth the root of army and state and spent lightly on nothing; rewards went only to families of the dead in merit—kin never received beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 臨敵常與士卒同在矢石之間，左右死傷者相繼，而帝神色自若，是以人思効命，所向無前。

translations.literal: Facing the enemy he was always with the soldiers amid arrows and stones; those beside him were wounded and killed in succession, yet the Emperor's expression was calm—therefore men wished to give their lives and wherever he turned nothing stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he stood with the soldiers under arrow and stone; aides fell beside him yet his face was calm—men gave their lives and nothing stood before him.

sentences.zh: 命將出師，指授節度，從命者無不制勝，違爽者率多敗失。

translations.literal: When he ordered generals forth he assigned strategy; those who obeyed were never not victorious; those who deviated mostly met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned strategy to generals; obedience won; deviation mostly lost.

sentences.zh: 性又知人，拔士於卒伍之中，惟其才效所長，不論本末。

translations.literal: By nature he also knew men and raised officers from the ranks, using only their talent and effectiveness without regard to origin.
translations.idiomatic: He knew men and raised officers from the ranks for talent alone, regardless of origin.

sentences.zh: 兼甚嚴斷，明於刑賞。

translations.literal: Moreover he was very stern and clear in punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and clear in punishments and rewards.

sentences.zh: 功者賞不遺賊；

translations.literal: The meritorious were rewarded without omitting even enemies;
translations.idiomatic: The meritorious were rewarded without omitting even enemies;

sentences.zh: 罪者刑不避親，雖寵愛之，終不虧法。

translations.literal: the guilty were punished without avoiding kin; even those he favored were never excused from the law.
translations.idiomatic: the guilty were punished without sparing kin; even favorites were never excused.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「法者，朕與天下共之，何敢輕也。

translations.literal: He often said: "The law is what We share with the realm—how dare We treat it lightly?"
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "The law is Ours with the realm—how dare We treat it lightly?"

sentences.zh: 」故大臣犯法，無所寬假。

translations.literal: Therefore when great ministers violated the law there was no indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers broke the law there was no indulgence.

sentences.zh: 雅長聽察，瞬息之間，下人無以措其姦隱。

translations.literal: He excelled at listening and observing; in an instant subordinates could not hide their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: He listened and observed keenly; in an instant subordinates could not hide treachery.

sentences.zh: 然果於誅戮，後多悔之。

translations.literal: Yet he was resolute in execution and afterward often repented.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was quick to kill and often repented afterward.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩既死之後，帝北伐，時宣城公李孝伯疾篤，傳者以為卒也。

translations.literal: After Chancellor of State Cui Hao died, the Emperor campaigned north; at that time Duke of Xuancheng Li Xiaobo was gravely ill and rumor said he had died.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Hao died the Emperor campaigned north; Li Xiaobo, Duke of Xuancheng, was gravely ill and rumor said he had died.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而悼之，謂左右曰：「李宣城可惜。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and mourned him, saying to those beside him: "Li of Xuancheng is to be regretted."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this he mourned and said: "Li of Xuancheng is to be regretted."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「朕向失言。

translations.literal: He also said: "We spoke wrongly before."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "We spoke wrongly before."

sentences.zh: 崔司徒可惜，李宣城可哀。

translations.literal: Cui the Chancellor is to be regretted; Li of Xuancheng is to be pitied."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Cui is to be regretted; Li of Xuancheng is to be pitied."

sentences.zh: 」褒貶雅意，皆此類也。

translations.literal: In praise and blame his refined intent was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His praise and blame were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 恭宗景穆皇帝諱晃，太武皇帝之長子也，母賀夫人。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingmu Gongzong bore the taboo name Huang; he was the Taiwu Emperor's eldest son; his mother was Lady He.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingmu Gongzong bore the taboo name Huang; he was the Taiwu Emperor's eldest son; his mother was Lady He.

sentences.zh: 延和元年春正月丙午，立為皇太子，時年五歲。

translations.literal: Yanhe year 1, spring, first month, day bingwu: he was established as Crown Prince at age five.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanhe year 1, on the bingwu day of the first month of spring, he was made Crown Prince at five.

sentences.zh: 明慧強識，聞則不忘。

translations.literal: Bright and intelligent with strong memory; what he heard he did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and strong of memory; he forgot nothing he heard.

sentences.zh: 及長，好讀經史，皆通大義。

translations.literal: When he grew he loved reading the classics and histories and all grasped their great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he loved the classics and histories and grasped their great meaning.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚奇之。

translations.literal: Shizu marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 世祖東征和龍，詔恭宗錄尚書事；

translations.literal: When Shizu campaigned east against Helong, an edict ordered Gongzong to record Secretariat affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu campaigned east on Helong, Gongzong was ordered to record Secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 西征涼州，詔恭宗監國。

translations.literal: when he campaigned west on Liangzhou, an edict ordered Gongzong to oversee the realm.
translations.idiomatic: when he campaigned west on Liangzhou, Gongzong was ordered to oversee the realm.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖之伐河西也，李順等咸言姑臧無水草，不可行師。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shizu campaigned on Hexi, Li Shun and others all said Guzang had no grass or water and an army could not march.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, campaigning on Hexi, Li Shun and others said Guzang had no grass or water and no army could march.

sentences.zh: 恭宗有疑色。

translations.literal: Gongzong showed doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzong looked doubtful.

sentences.zh: 及車駕至姑臧，乃詔恭宗曰：「姑臧城東西門外涌泉合於城北，其大如河。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Guzang, an edict was sent to Gongzong: "East and west of Guzang city spring water joins north of the city, large as a river.
translations.idiomatic: At Guzang he edicted Gongzong: "East and west of Guzang springs join north of the city, large as a river.

sentences.zh: 自餘溝渠流入澤中，其間乃無燥地。

translations.literal: The rest flow through ditches into marshes; between them there is no dry ground.
translations.idiomatic: Ditches flow into marshes; between them is no dry ground.

sentences.zh: 澤草茂盛，可供大軍數年。

translations.literal: Marsh grass is lush and can supply a great army for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Marsh grass is lush and can feed a great army for years.

sentences.zh: 人之多言，亦可惡也。

translations.literal: Much talk by men is also hateful.
translations.idiomatic: Men's much talk is hateful too.

sentences.zh: 故有此敕，以釋汝疑。

translations.literal: Therefore this edict, to dispel your doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Hence this edict to dispel your doubt."

sentences.zh: 」恭宗謂宮臣曰：「為人臣不實若此，豈是忠乎！

translations.literal: Gongzong said to the palace ministers: "To be a minister so untrue as this—is this loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Gongzong told palace ministers: "A minister so untrue—is this loyalty?

sentences.zh: 吾初聞有疑，但帝決行耳。

translations.literal: When I first heard I had doubt, but the Emperor had decided to march.
translations.idiomatic: I doubted at first, but the Emperor had decided to march.

sentences.zh: 幾誤人大事，言者復何面見帝也。」

translations.literal: Nearly to err in a great matter—how can the speakers face the Emperor again?"
translations.idiomatic: Nearly to err in a great matter—how can the speakers face the Emperor again?"

sentences.zh: 真君四年，恭宗從世祖討蠕蠕，至鹿渾谷，與賊相遇，虜惶怖，部落擾亂。

translations.literal: Zhenjun year 4: Gongzong followed Shizu against the Rouran to Luhun Valley; they met the enemy; the barbarians were fearful and the tribes were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun year 4 Gongzong followed Shizu against the Rouran to Luhun Valley; they met the enemy; the tribes were thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 恭宗言於世祖曰：「今大軍卒至，宜速進擊，奄其不備，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Gongzong said to Shizu: "Now the great army has come suddenly; we should press the attack swiftly and take them unawares—breaking them is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Gongzong said: "The great army has come suddenly; press the attack and take them unawares—victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 」尚書令劉潔固諫，以為塵盛賊多，出至平地，恐為所圍，須軍大集，然後擊之可也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Liu Jie firmly remonstrated, holding that the dust was great and the enemy many; if they went out to level ground they might be surrounded; the army must gather in full before striking.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie, Minister of Works, remonstrated: the dust was great and enemies many; on level ground they might be surrounded; wait for the full host.

sentences.zh: 恭宗謂潔曰：「此塵之盛，由賊恇擾，軍人亂故，何有營上而有此塵？

translations.literal: Gongzong said to Jie: "This dust is great because the enemy are frightened and the soldiers are in disorder—how could there be such dust over a camp?"
translations.idiomatic: Gongzong said: "The dust is from enemy panic and soldier disorder—how dust over a camp?"

sentences.zh: 」世祖疑之，遂不急擊，蠕蠕遠遁。

translations.literal: Shizu doubted and did not press the attack swiftly; the Rouran fled far.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu doubted and did not press; the Rouran fled far.

sentences.zh: 既而獲虜候騎，世祖問之，對曰：「蠕蠕不覺官軍卒至，上下惶懼，引眾北走，經六七日，知無追者，始乃徐行。

translations.literal: Later Rouran scouts were captured; Shizu questioned them; they replied: "The Rouran did not know the army had come suddenly; all were fearful and led the host north; after six or seven days, knowing there was no pursuit, they went slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Captured scouts said: "The Rouran did not know the army had come; all fled north; after six or seven days without pursuit they went slowly."

sentences.zh: 」世祖深恨之，自是恭宗所言軍國大事，多見納用，遂知萬機。

translations.literal: Shizu deeply regretted it; from then on Gongzong's words on army and state were mostly adopted and he came to know the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu deeply regretted it; thereafter Gongzong's counsel on army and state was mostly followed and he came to know the myriad affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，恭宗監國，曾令曰：「周書言：『任農以耕事，貢九穀；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gongzong oversaw the realm, he issued an order: "The Zhou Documents say: 'Entrust the farmer with plowing and tribute of the nine grains;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, overseeing the realm, he ordered: "The Zhou Documents say: 'Entrust the farmer with plowing and tribute of the nine grains;

sentences.zh: 任圃以樹事，貢草木；

translations.literal: entrust the gardener with trees and tribute of plants and trees;
translations.idiomatic: entrust the gardener with trees and tribute of plants;

sentences.zh: 任工以餘材，貢器物；

translations.literal: entrust the artisan with surplus materials and tribute of vessels;
translations.idiomatic: entrust the artisan with surplus materials and tribute of vessels;

sentences.zh: [6]任商以市事，貢貨賄；

translations.literal: [6] entrust the merchant with market affairs and tribute of goods and wealth;
translations.idiomatic: [6] entrust the merchant with market affairs and tribute of goods;

sentences.zh: 任牧以畜事，貢鳥獸；

translations.literal: entrust the herdsman with livestock and tribute of birds and beasts;
translations.idiomatic: entrust the herdsman with livestock and tribute of birds and beasts;

sentences.zh: 任嬪以女事，貢布帛；

translations.literal: entrust the consort with women's work and tribute of cloth and silk;
translations.idiomatic: entrust the consort with women's work and tribute of cloth;

sentences.zh: 任衡以山事，貢其材；

translations.literal: entrust the forest officer with mountain affairs and tribute of its materials;
translations.idiomatic: entrust the forest officer with mountain affairs and tribute of materials;

sentences.zh: 任虞以澤事，貢其物。

translations.literal: entrust the park officer with marsh affairs and tribute of its products.'
translations.idiomatic: entrust the park officer with marsh affairs and tribute of its products.'

sentences.zh: 』其制有司課畿內之民，使無牛家以人牛力相貿，墾殖鋤耨。

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices assess the people within the capital region, making households without cattle exchange human and bovine labor to open fields, hoe, and weed.
translations.idiomatic: Let offices assess the capital region, having households without cattle exchange human and ox labor to open fields.

sentences.zh: 其有牛家與無牛家一人種田二十二畝，償以私鋤功七畝，[7]如是為差，至與小、老無牛家種田七畝，小、老者償以鋤功二畝。

translations.literal: Where there is a cattle household and a household without cattle, one person plants twenty-two mu and is compensated with seven mu of private hoeing labor, [7] with gradations accordingly; for small and elderly households without cattle, seven mu are planted and small and elderly repay with two mu of hoeing.
translations.idiomatic: Where one has cattle and one does not, one person plants twenty-two mu for seven mu of hoeing, [7] by gradation; small and elderly without cattle plant seven mu and repay two mu.

sentences.zh: 皆以五口下貧家為率。

translations.literal: All take households of five mouths or fewer in poverty as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: All take poor households of five mouths or fewer as standard.

sentences.zh: 各列家別口數，所勸種頃畝，明立簿目。

translations.literal: Each lists households by mouth count and urged planting in mu, clearly setting ledger accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Each lists households, urged planting, and sets ledgers.

sentences.zh: 所種者於地首標題姓名，以辨播殖之功。

translations.literal: What is planted is marked at the field head with name to distinguish sowing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Planters mark the field head with names to distinguish merit.

sentences.zh: 」又禁飲酒、雜戲、棄本沽販者。

translations.literal: " He also forbade drinking, mixed games, and abandoning the root to peddle for profit.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade drinking, mixed games, and peddling over farming.

sentences.zh: 墾田大為增闢。

translations.literal: Opened fields were greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: Opened fields greatly increased.

sentences.zh: 正平元年六月戊辰，薨於東宮，時年二十四。

translations.literal: Zhengping year 1, sixth month, day wuchen: he died in the Eastern Palace at age twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengping year 1, on the wuchen day of the sixth month, he died in the Eastern Palace at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 庚午，冊曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: Day gengwu: the patent of enfeoffment said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day the patent said: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 惟爾誕資明叡，岐嶷夙成。

translations.literal: You were born with bright wisdom and precocious insight from youth.
translations.idiomatic: You were born bright and precocious from youth.

sentences.zh: 正位少陽，克荷基構。

translations.literal: You took the position of the young yang and bore the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: You took the young yang and bore the foundation.

sentences.zh: 賓于四門，百揆時叙；

translations.literal: Guest at the four gates, the hundred duties were in order;
translations.idiomatic: Guest at the four gates, the hundred duties were ordered;

sentences.zh: 允釐庶績，風雨不迷。

translations.literal: you truly regulated the myriad tasks; wind and rain did not go astray.
translations.idiomatic: you regulated the myriad tasks; wind and rain did not stray.

sentences.zh: 宜享無疆，隆我皇祚，如何不幸，奄焉殂殞，朕用悲慟于厥心！

translations.literal: You should have enjoyed boundless years and elevated Our royal fortune—how is it that misfortune came and you suddenly died? We are stricken with grief in Our heart!
translations.idiomatic: You should have enjoyed boundless years—how misfortune came and you died! We are stricken in heart!

sentences.zh: 今使使持節兼太尉張黎、兼司徒竇瑾奉策，即柩賜諡曰『景穆』，以顯昭令德。

translations.literal: Now We send the credential-bearing commissioner Concurrent Grand Commandant Zhang Li and Concurrent Chancellor of State Dou Jin with the patent to grant at the bier the posthumous title "Jingmu," to display your bright virtue.
translations.idiomatic: We send Zhang Li, Concurrent Grand Commandant, and Dou Jin, Concurrent Chancellor of State, to grant at the bier the posthumous title Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，其尚嘉之。

translations.literal: If your soul has awareness, honor this."
translations.idiomatic: If your soul has awareness, honor this."

sentences.zh: 」高宗即位，追尊為景穆皇帝，廟號恭宗。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he posthumously honored him as Emperor Jingmu Gongzong; temple name Gongzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne he honored him as Emperor Jingmu Gongzong; temple name Gongzong.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：世祖聰明雄斷，威靈傑立，藉二世之資，奮征伐之氣，遂戎軒四出，周旋險夷。

translations.literal: The historian says: Shizu was intelligent, heroic, and resolute, majestic and outstanding; with the resources of two reigns he roused the spirit of conquest and then the war chariot went forth on four sides, turning through peril and ease.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Shizu was intelligent, heroic, and resolute; with two reigns' resources he roused conquest; the war chariot went four ways through peril and ease.

sentences.zh: 掃統萬，平秦隴，翦遼海，盪河源，南夷荷擔，北蠕削跡，廓定四表，混一戎華，其為功也大矣。

translations.literal: He swept Tongwan, pacified Qin and Long, cut Liaohai, cleared the river source; southern barbarians bore burdens, northern Rouran were cut down; the four quarters were settled and barbarian and Chinese were unified—his achievement was great.
translations.idiomatic: He swept Tongwan, pacified Qin and Long, cut Liaohai, cleared the river source; south bore burdens, north Rouran were cut; the four quarters were settled and barbarian and Chinese unified—his achievement was great.

sentences.zh: 遂使有魏之業，光邁百王，豈非神叡經綸，事當命世。

translations.literal: Thus the enterprise of Wei shone beyond the hundred kings—is this not divine wisdom and planning, a mandate for the age?
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wei's enterprise shone beyond the hundred kings—is this not divine wisdom and a mandate for the age?

sentences.zh: 至於初則東儲不終，末乃釁成所忽。

translations.literal: Yet at the start the eastern heir did not reach the end; at the last a breach arose from what was neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the start the eastern heir did not finish; at the last breach arose from neglect.

sentences.zh: 固本貽防，殆弗思乎？

translations.literal: To secure the root and leave forethought—was this not unconsidered?
translations.idiomatic: To secure the root and leave forethought—was this unconsidered?

translations.literal: According to the so-called "exchange of human and bovine labor," that is, cattle households exchange bovine labor for human labor; "one person" should read "one ox," and "private" should also read "weeding."
translations.idiomatic: By "exchange of human and bovine labor," cattle households trade ox labor for human labor; "one person" should be "one ox" and "private" should be "weeding."

sentences.zh: 意謂有牛家出牛一頭，為無牛家耕種二十或二十二畝；

translations.literal: The meaning is that a cattle household puts forth one ox to plant twenty or twenty-two mu for a household without cattle;
translations.idiomatic: A cattle household puts forth one ox to plant twenty or twenty-two mu for a household without cattle;

sentences.zh: 無牛家出人，為有牛家耘鋤七畝以為報償。

translations.literal: the household without cattle puts forth men to weed and hoe seven mu for the cattle household as repayment.
translations.idiomatic: the household without cattle puts forth men to weed seven mu for the cattle household as repayment.
